chunks: ʿAlī, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Rizq Allāh, from Badr, the غلام of Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, who said:

I came to al-Jabal while I did not hold to the Imamate; I loved them as a whole, until Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh died. During his illness he bequeathed that al-Shihrī al-Samand, his sword, and his belt be delivered to his Mawlā.

So I feared that if I did not hand over al-Shihrī to Idhkūtakīn, I would suffer belittlement from him. So I appraised the animal, the sword, and the belt at seven hundred dinars within myself and informed no one of it. Then a letter came to me from al-ʿIrāq: 'Send the seven hundred dinars which are due to us from you, from the price of al-Shihrī, the sword, and the belt.'

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest during illness or before death
key_terms.الشِّهْرِيُّ: the named horse mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the doctrine and authority of the Imam
key_terms.الْكِتَابُ: the written message that arrived from al-ʿIrāq
key_terms.الْمِنْطَقَةَ: the belt or girdle included with the bequeathed items
key_terms.سَبْعَ مِائَةَ دِينَارٍ: the appraised value of the items
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, referring here to the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith present a sign of the Imam's knowledge concerning privately assessed property?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in which a man was entrusted with property to be delivered to the Imam, yet due to fear of a political authority he internally assessed its value instead. A letter then arrived from al-ʿIrāq specifying the exact amount he had privately determined, serving in the narrative as a sign connected to the Imam and the doctrine of Imamate.
